steps.content: Few undamaged areas remain within the manor. You use the rocky terrain for cover, locating a temporary hiding spot.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: They're distracted for the moment, but that won't last. How're you holding up?

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: I didn't expect it to be you outside... I had to forcibly stop my meditation, and the energy backlash... ugh...
She clenches her teeth as fresh blood seeps from the corner of her mouth.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You're in no shape to fight anyone, even if you do manage to recover. What's the plan?

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: I have to try. I still have some... unfinished business...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Something you still can't tell me about?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Fine. Then I'll figure it out myself. Whatever you've been scheming this whole time, I'll get to the bottom of it. But first, we actually have to survive.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: We're not winning this in a fair fight. The only chance is getting out of the manor. Any paths down the mountain still open?
Shuang'er coughs out a laugh.

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: None... The back mountain path was crushed by an avalanche, and the front gate is sealed shut too... This whole place was designed as a trap from the start.
She closes her eyes, her silence radiating an almost stubborn resolve.
You stop pressing her for answers, focusing instead on the enemy's movements. In this brief silence, you feel her gaze on you.

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: But there is a way... one that could at least save you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...Yeah, I know. Those other heroes already gave me the same offer.

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: Since you know... why haven't you?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Because I also know that even if I helped you right now, it wouldn't change much. We'd still be in the same mess.
Shuang'er freezes in shock.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Look, I'm not from Northwild. I don't have your fancy martial arts, and I don't know all the rules of your world.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But I've got eyes. I saw the real evidence of what happened at the manor. I can tell right from wrong when I look at those charges. And I already know exactly what kind of people are making them. Even if I switched sides, they wouldn't exactly welcome me with open arms.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: More importantly, I know you're not behind those three incidents. Whatever you're actually after, you don't deserve to get handed over to them on false charges.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If something's right, and someone needs help, and I'm in a position to do something, I can't just walk away. Even if... all I can manage is buying you a few more minutes.
You hold yourself alert to outside dangers, your voice perfectly calm.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The only reason I keep asking about your plans is that I need to know: is helping you the right call? Behind all the lies and secrets, are you actually the kind of person Shuang'er wants to be, the kind with real honor?
A half-stick of incense passes as she regulates her breathing, yet Shuang'er still feels something inside her refuse to settle.
Ten years ago, beneath the candy shop at the town entrance, a similar fire once burned.
It surged through her, fierce and consuming.
[Memory Fragment]

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Have they left...?

steps.speaker: Mudling
steps.content: Nope. Still circling up ahead... What'd you do to make 'em this mad?

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: They... they overturned Uncle Zhang's bun stall. Sent his buns rolling everywhere. Wouldn't pay, wouldn't apologize. Just threatened to beat him instead. I... I couldn't just stand there. I told them I'd cover the cost, but they had to apologize to Uncle Zhang first.

steps.speaker: Mudling
steps.content: I knew it! Scabby Wang and his pack. They bully this street like they own it. Someone oughta teach 'em a real lesson!

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Don't! There are too many of them... You should go. I don't want you caught up in this because of me.

steps.speaker: Mudling
steps.content: What's there to be scared of? These fists don't know the meaning of the word! Hey, didn't I just haul you over here like it was nothing?

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: You're amazing... I'm not like you. All I did was run my mouth and nearly make things worse... My tutors always say I'm meant to take charge of the manor one day and help people. But I can't even help myself...

steps.speaker: Mudling
steps.content: Who says?! You stood up to them. Told 'em to apologize. In front of everyone! That takes guts. That's what they call... uh... speaking up for what's right! Me? I've just got muscle. Couldn't come up with words like that if I tried.

steps.speaker: Mudling
steps.content: And back there, if you hadn't spotted this broken basket pile, I'd still be running in circles, and they'd have caught me ages ago.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: That's just a little cleverness. It doesn't really do anything...

steps.speaker: Mudling
steps.content: That's not true! I've got strength; I can chase off the bad guys. You've got a sharp mind; you can see the way out when no one else can. Big fist or little fist, a fist that protects someone is a good fist. That's all there is to it.

steps.speaker: Mudling
steps.content: You've got what you're good at. I've got what I'm good at. And if I'm gonna be Ping'an Town's number one hero, you can be number two!

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: You want to be a hero?

steps.speaker: Mudling
steps.content: Just a small goal, no big deal. You could be one too! Real strength doesn't come from fists, anyway. It comes from here—

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Your heart?

steps.speaker: Mudling
steps.content: When there's a fire in here, people you wanna protect, things you wanna make right, that's when the strength shows up. You got people like that? Things you wanna do?

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: I'm... not sure yet. My tutors want me to lead Northsnow Manor. To make our name mean something again. To be the kind of manor master who helps people, the way my parents did.

steps.speaker: Mudling
steps.content: Well, I know what I'm for! Whenever I see someone in this town getting pushed around—don't matter why—I step in. Figure out the rest later.

steps.speaker: Mudling
steps.content: Then I'll just go "whoosh," jump right in front of 'em, and shout: "Bullying the helpless in broad daylight? No shame?!" And then wham, bam, down they go!

steps.speaker: Mudling
steps.content: Heh, I got a little carried away... They're coming. You should go first.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: Wait, what's your name?

steps.speaker: Mudling
steps.content: No folks. No family. Nothing to lose. I'm scruffy, sure, but I don't break when I fall, and I don't stay down when I'm kicked. Folks around here just call me Mudling.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: When will I see you again?

steps.speaker: Mudling
steps.content: Let's make it a deal. When I'm a real big hero, and you're a real great manor master!
[Back to Reality]
The half-incense meditation period comes to an end, and Jichuan opens her eyes.

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: Remember, do not channel your internal force unless you have no other choice. These final treatments are fighting poison with poison, using fire to sustain a flame that's already guttering. Any strength you feel now is borrowed. When the oil runs dry, the lamp goes out... That much is certain.

steps.speaker: Jichuan
steps.content: How much time do I have?

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: If you use this method to mask your condition and preserve your life force, three months, perhaps. But if you push further, if you force your exertion in combat... your meridians will crumble in as little as three days.

Jichuan turns her head. The pale winter sunlight does little to hide the anxious sweat on the other person's face, sweat earned while protecting her. She keeps count; in just a few short days, she has gone against the doctor's orders three times.

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: The grand banquet... even with the illusion, I had to let a thread of internal force slip to fool those old foxes. That was the first.

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: To escape from Doctor Yin's grasp... I had no choice but to use my martial arts again... That was another time.

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: But that poison fog trap... I still don't know why I rushed in...

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: Too many tales from down the mountain. Too many storytelling benches... Somewhere along the way, I started believing I was one of them, the fool who runs in to save people when no one else will.

But isn't the person before her committing the same foolish act? This is the other side of the martial world: not just schemes and slaughter, but the choice to intervene when witnessing injustice, the choice to do what must be done despite knowing it's impossible. Even when strength is lacking, the will to protect something, to prove something, still burns.
But at this moment, unlike him, she still has this withered branch in her hand—one that can cut through the wind in battle.
steps.female_content: But at this moment, unlike her, she still has this withered branch in her hand—one that can cut through the wind in battle.

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: Young hero, they'll find this place soon enough. But I have a way out.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I thought you said the manor was completely sealed off?

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: East cliff, in the mist, there's an old plum tree. Beneath it lies a passage, the last resort I saved. Activating it will take a moment... and it won't be quiet... Cough, cough...

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: You're right. In my current state, if those three corner us, I can't guarantee we'll both make it. So I need you. Someone to execute the "big fist and little fist" move with me.

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: That old friend of mine taught me... Mudling was a rare one in Northwild, born with the strength of a true hero. She used to say: fists big as clay pots and fists little as peas, each has its place.

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: Back when I had no martial arts to speak of, I'd step forward, bluff and bluster, lure the troublemakers right where we wanted them... and Mudling, hidden nearby, would spring out and catch them completely off guard.

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: She told me weeds and plum blossoms grow from the same soil. No hierarchy between them. But once you've got the strength to break through frozen ground, taking root to stand guard isn't just a choice anymore. It's a responsibility.
You have heard her mention that old friend once before, but this is the first time you are learning that Northwild has such a natural-born hero.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So you want me to be the bait.

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: No, not bait. I need you to be my eyes and voice. Not just to draw them out, but also to mislead, to maneuver. Use what you're good at: observation, judgment, and talking. Keep them busy and buy me a moment.
She reaches out and gently brushes the hair before your eyes, clearing your field of vision.

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: I know that most of what I've told you has been lies. My name. My identity. Even these martial arts I wield... they're wrapped in deception too.

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: I've exploited your kindness, dragged you into this mess, and put you in harm's way. I won't deny any of it.

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: But one thing I never lied about.
With a tight grip on her stick, she uses it to lever herself up from the corner.

steps.speaker: Shuang'er
steps.content: For once, I want to be a real hero. I want to help the people of Northwild. I want the heavy snow on this land... to stop.
